claim: Incubation breaks give a small, reliable benefit on insight-type problems (weighted d about 0.29; unweighted 0.41), but the effect depends on the break task: undemanding interpolated tasks beat rest or demanding tasks.
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare: continue on the impasse vs park it and do an unrelated low-load subtask (or fresh re-sample with context reset) vs same-length continued CoT. Measure solve rate on RAT or BrainTeaser-style items.

claim: Incubation helps most when a misleading cue (fixation) was present in preparation; this supports forgetting or relaxing the wrong set as the mechanism. Effect is clear for linguistic problems (0.36 vs 0.17) and not for visual ones.
agent_test: Plant a misleading hint in the prompt; test whether dropping the hint-bearing context at the impasse (O6) beats keeping it, at equal tokens.

claim: Insight problems are solved by relaxing self-imposed constraints; wide-scope constraints are harder and relaxing them transfers to later problems of the same type (matchstick Exp 1A N=20, Exp 1B N=38, Exp 2 N=78). Boundary: the add-on that physical interaction helps restructuring failed to replicate (Spiridonov 2026, N=105/88/73); movement hurt relaxing high-level constraints.
agent_test: At an impasse, force the agent to list its implicit constraints and drop one at a time (widest scope first); compare with unstructured retry at equal tokens.

claim: Aha ratings track correctness only loosely: correct solutions score higher (66.5 vs 52.3, t(69)=10.21) but 37% of wrong solutions (417 of 1124) rated above the correct mean, so a felt Aha is not a verification signal.
agent_test: Compare agent sudden-confidence with independent verification on wrong answers; check whether an S8 check that ignores felt certainty catches the false insights.

claim: Insight solutions are more often correct than non-insight ones on classic insight items (Aha-accuracy r about 0.40-0.50), but this is partly metacognitive and task-dependent, not a clean process marker.
agent_test: Use agent confidence jump (token-level or self-rating) as a predictor of correctness on insight items vs analytic items; report AUC.

claim: Insight solutions are remembered better one week later than wrong ones (57.7% vs 35.4% recalled, correct vs wrong), partly via surprise and restructuring.
agent_test: Store insight-flagged solutions with their restructuring step in memory; test reuse on later related tasks vs plain answer storage.

claim: In reasoning LLMs, mid-trace Aha shifts are rare (6.31% of traces; formal detector 1.79%) and go with lower accuracy (pooled 6.6% vs 29.0%), so spontaneous self-reported restructuring is not a sign of better reasoning.
agent_test: Count restructuring phrases in our agent traces and correlate with correctness; do not reward them.

claim: Triggering an extrinsic reconsideration pass under high uncertainty improves accuracy (MATH-500 32.21% to 40.62%, +8.41 pp; 50,574 wrong-to-right vs 23,500 right-to-wrong), but nothing on crosswords or Rush Hour (+0.45, +0.01 pp). Two passes cost more tokens; an equal-token control is missing.
agent_test: Entropy-triggered second pass vs matched best-of-2 at equal tokens on math and puzzle items.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 by round 2); oracle labels help, so the gain comes from the external signal.
agent_test: S8 verification must use an independent check (tool, second context, or constraint test), not the same context re-reading its answer; compare at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs lag humans on insight-type riddles: Nazonazo reasoning models 17.6% vs humans 52.9% (non-reasoning 7.6%); BRAINTEASER best ChatGPT 53/63% vs 92% (3 experts, 102 items); Only Connect GPT-3.5/4 near zero until red herrings removed.
agent_test: Run our agent on Nazonazo-like and BRAINTEASER items with a plain baseline vs scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: Models often produce the right answer in their reasoning log but then reject or overwrite it: verification failures are 5.23% to 39.34% of wrong answers (Gemini 2.5 Flash to Grok 4).
agent_test: Log every candidate answer produced during the run; score all candidates with a separate verifier and pick the best, vs last-answer.

claim: Fixation on red herrings or familiar shortcuts is measurable in LLMs: removing red herrings lifts Only Connect from single digits to hundreds of 494 walls; mental-set tests show CoT helps on shortcut problems.
agent_test: Add a misleading but plausible cue to items; measure the drop and whether an O6 drop-the-cue step recovers it.

claim: LLM results on classic insight problems are mixed: ChatGPT 12/30 (modal human) in Orru; GPT-4 4.5/5 in Speed (single observation); Jiang finds a large gap. Contamination and small samples likely explain the inconsistency.
agent_test: Use fresh, post-cutoff items only; report with item-level variance.

claim: Search plus pruning beats linear chain-of-thought where a dead end must be abandoned: Game of 24 GPT-4 CoT 4% vs Tree of Thoughts 74%.
agent_test: Compare backtrack-on-stall with linear CoT at equal token budget on Game-of-24-like tasks.

claim: A structural restructuring scaffold can lift LLM accuracy (context graph 73.3% to 93.9% on restructuring trials, n=30 vs 33, p=0.038), but the study is small and uses one model family.
agent_test: Replicate with our own constraint-graph prompt on held-out items at equal tokens.

claim: Neural signature: right anterior superior temporal gyrus activity is higher for insight than non-insight solutions (peak 0.25% signal difference, 12 of 13 subjects), pointing to a discrete shift in distant semantic integration. Small N, no LLM analogue.
agent_test: None directly; at best, test whether remote-association retrieval (sampling distant concepts) helps at impasse.

claim: The four-stage Wallas/Hadamard model is descriptive with weak direct evidence for each stage; impasse is not always a prerequisite for insight solutions and restructuring also occurs in non-insight solving.
agent_test: Ablate the impasse trigger: restructure at fixed intervals vs only on detected stall, at equal tokens.

claim: Cross-family verification beats self-verification and same-family verification (37 models, 9 benchmarks); self-verification gain is smallest, and reasoning post-training weakens it. Qwen3 and DeepSeek already self-verify spontaneously in 96% and 73% of outputs.
agent_test: On wrong-then-rejected cases, compare same-model re-check vs a different-family verifier at equal total tokens.

claim: At a fixed inference budget, more independent attempts (self-consistency) beat generative verification until about 8x compute; verification gains 3.8% only at about 128x extra compute (math).
agent_test: Equal-token arm: N attempts + vote vs fewer attempts + verifier chain on riddle items.

claim: Entropy-based and loop-based signals work as 'stop or intervene' detectors: EAT cuts tokens 12-22% with no accuracy loss; TrigReason loop trigger lifts AIME24 accuracy; high-entropy transition tokens flag drift. None is validated as an impasse classifier for restructuring.
agent_test: Label stalled vs productive spans on a held-out set and report precision and recall for entropy, repetition, hesitation words and step count.

claim: Repeated-answer rate is a weak correctness and impasse signal: self-consistent errors do not shrink with model size and evade consistency, probability and probe detectors.
agent_test: Check how often repeated wrong answers occur on riddle items; use an external check rather than agreement.

claim: The matchstick interactivity effect did not replicate in three experiments (N=105, 88, 73); no failed replication of the core constraint-hierarchy result was found.
agent_test: None for the agent directly; do not credit acting on the problem as a restructuring aid without a test.

claim: No LLM study of incubation, context reset or parked subproblem on RAT items was located; indirect evidence says fresh restarts lose where state must be carried (long chain beats many short ones on graph connectivity).
agent_test: Run the equal-token incubation test from K01 on compound-RAT items with a no-break control.

claim: Strategy memory from successes and failures helps agent reuse (WebArena +4.6 to +8.3 points), but agents often ignore condensed experience, so a stored restructuring note needs a causal-use check.
agent_test: Store insight flag + raw solution + note; perturb the note and measure behaviour change.

claim: Carried-over fixation from earlier problems is not clearly shown in LLMs (tiny N=6 per cell, order effect reversed for GPT-4o); fixation by in-context red herrings is the measured form. No post-2025 frontier-model measurement was found.
agent_test: Plant a misleading hint, measure the accuracy penalty on a frontier reasoning model, then test context drop.
